scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS asks for an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (a hypothesis to test, not the problem).
symptoms: Monthly disputes rose from 610 (Jun) and 590 (Jul) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-01).
1240 of 3025 disputed bills are ESTIMATED reads and 1785 are ACTUAL reads (E-04).
Route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target in Aug–Sep, covering 9200 manual-read accounts (E-05).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month (Jun–Jul) to 1180–1260 (Aug–Sep) while response times are within SLA, so the cause lies upstream in bill accuracy. Best-supported mechanism: manual reads are missed or late (route completion 0.88 vs 0.95, 9200 manual-read accounts), so billing substitutes estimates, and estimated bills drive part of the disputes (1240 of 3025). Estimates do not explain the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes, which remain a separate open cause.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a ticket-handling and response-speed problem that an auto-answer agent would resolve.

H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A billing import validation rule change around August rejects valid reads. This causes more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-AMI-FEED-DEFECT.statement: The AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) is dropping, delaying or mis-mapping register reads. Billing then substitutes estimates.

H-FIELD-READ-GAP.statement: Manual reads are being missed or uploaded late (H-FIELD-BILL) because of route completion gaps or staffing. This causes estimated bills and disputes.

H-MULTI-FACTOR.statement: Several causes combine, such as rule changes, feed defects and field gaps. Different customer segments are affected by different causes.

H-ACTUAL-READ-WRONG.statement: Many disputed bills use ACTUAL reads, so wrong bills may come from misapplied, mis-mapped or invalid actual reads, or from customer misunderstanding.

H-FIRMWARE-HIGHCONS.statement: AMI firmware v4.2 produces reads that billing flags as high consumption, so valid reads are rejected and estimates substituted.

H-UNIT-SCALING-MISMATCH.statement: Firmware v4.2 reports register values in a different unit or scale than the 12-month m3 history. BV-17 compares them without scaling, so valid reads are rejected as high consumption.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Monthly disputes were about 600 in June and July, then about doubled to 1180 in August and 1260 in September (E-01). This confirms the surge and its timing, but not its cause or any link to response speed.
Tickets are answered quickly: median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA (E-02). Slow handling therefore does not explain the doubling of dispute volume.

The billing tariff change log has no records, so no tariff change is recorded that could explain wrong bills or the August surge (E-03). It says nothing about import validation rules, which sit in a separate log (DA-RULES).
Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 are ESTIMATED and 1785 are ACTUAL reads (E-04). Estimation is a major contributor but not most disputes, so no single estimate-driven cause explains the surge.

Route completion was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over Aug–Sep, with 9200 manual-read accounts (E-05). This shows a field read gap exists, but not whether it began in August or how much of the dispute surge it explains.

Route completion of 0.88 against a 0.95 target in Aug–Sep with 9200 manual-read accounts still shows a field read gap. Given E-12, it explains at most a small share of estimates (56 of 1240 had no read received) and is not the main cause of the disputes.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

SH-FIELD's claim of a three-reader shortage since July remains an unverified, non-authoritative statement. It does not explain most disputed estimates, which came from AMI import rejection (E-12), and it gives no support for staffing as the cause.

Of 1240 disputed estimated bills, 1184 had an AMI read before cutoff that was exported but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (firmware v4.2). Only 56 had no read received, so most estimates come from import rejection, not missed field reads.

U-VALIDATION-RULES.question: Did a billing import validation rule change around August reject valid reads (H-VALIDATION-RULE-CHANGE)? The rule log DA-RULES has not been queried.

proposal.summary: Disputes rose from about 600/month (Jun–Jul) to 1180–1260 (Aug–Sep) while responses met SLA, so the cause is upstream in bill accuracy, not ticket handling (E-01, E-02). The best-supported mechanism is that rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01) compares raw register values to m3 history without unit scaling, while firmware v4.2 reports 0.1 m3. Valid AMI reads are then rejected as high consumption and billed as estimates: 1184 of 1240 disputed estimates, confirmed by three independent sources (E-12, E-13, E-14, E-15, E-16, E-17). The original field-staffing explanation was invalidated by E-12. The release is narrow, read-only analysis of the MDMS-to-billing handoff, with a BV-17 unit-scaling recommendation to SH-BILL and the affected-account list for Billing Operations. It is released with known limitations because three verification obligations stay open but lie outside the release scope.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1 v2): the surge follows from BV-17 rejecting v4.2 reads, which are estimated instead. This replaces the earlier field-gap definition, which E-12 invalidated.
SH-CS's request for an auto-answer agent was treated as a hypothesis. It was rejected: responses were within SLA, median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA (E-02).

Establishing the cause: 1184 of 1240 disputed estimates had an AMI read exported but rejected as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION on v4.2, and only 56 had no read (E-12). billing-db and mdms-export independently match this count (E-15, E-16, E-17). BV-17 has no unit scaling (E-13), and v4.2 reports 0.1 m3 (E-14).
The tariff change log is empty (E-03), and SH-BILL says there was no tariff change (E-06). The import rule log was the right place to look, and it showed BV-17 (E-13).

Released: read-only analysis of the H-MDMS-BILL handoff, the affected-account list for Billing Operations (W-WI-AFFECTED-LIST), and a recommendation to SH-BILL to amend or roll back BV-17 (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX). No bill writes or route pushes are made (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH).

Decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds. The DEFINE Gate was CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the open VOB-U-ACTUAL-READS, VOB-U-UNIT-CONFIRM and VOB-U-BILL-AUTHORITY block only actions outside the release scope.
Field-gap and AMI-feed-defect hypotheses were rejected (H-FIELD-READ-GAP, H-AMI-FEED-DEFECT). Route completion of 0.88 against 0.95 is real (E-05) but explains at most the 56 no-read estimates.
limitations_explained: It is not yet shown that unit scaling would make the 1184 rejected reads pass BV-17. The fleet-wide number of v4.2 meters, including undisputed bills, is also unknown (U-UNIT-CONFIRM, VOB-U-UNIT-CONFIRM).
1785 disputed bills are ACTUAL reads, and their cause is unexplained (E-04, U-ACTUAL-READS, H-ACTUAL-READ-WRONG). The BV-17 finding does not cover them.
The holder of authority to re-bill or credit affected bills is unknown (U-BILL-AUTHORITY). Bill corrections stay manual and outside this solution (A-NO-BILL-WRITE).

The root cause is removed only if SH-BILL adopts the BV-17 fix (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX). Change control for validation rules (SR-RULE-CHANGE-CONTROL) is not feasible in the contest time, and DA-RULES has no named owner.
SH-AMI's claim that MDMS export access is provisioned is unverified as a stakeholder claim (E-11, CL-04). Tool reads from mdms-export did return data (E-17).
The pre-August estimated-bill baseline is unknown. It is also unexplained why 3025 disputed bills exceed the monthly ticket counts (U-BASELINE-MEASURE).

The timing link is an assumption: v4.2 rolled out in June but the surge began in August, consistent with BV-17 deployment (A-ONSET-BV17). No test yet applies unit scaling to the rejected reads (A-REJECT-IS-UNIT).
H-MULTI-FACTOR needs re-evaluation, and several success criteria and metrics from the earlier problem need confirmation against the successor problem (DR-1).
